S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. The manufacturer must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident presents a credible ongoing safety risk, and otherwise within 10 business days. Reports must include known circumstances, model and unit identifiers, injuries or damage, and any immediate safety action. Suspected under-reporting must be corrected promptly; reporting obligations apply regardless of whether the cause is confirmed.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% is a safety action level, not an automatic sales ban: the manufacturer must report it to the regulator within 5 business days and submit a regulator-approved corrective-action plan and retesting schedule. Continued sale during remediation may be allowed with regulator approval and adequate interim protections; permanent market exclusion requires a separate determination that corrective action cannot adequately control the risk. Per-model test results and supporting data must be submitted confidentially to the regulator and disclosed to customers who buy or are considering that model; public reporting must be limited to aggregated industry data that does not identify a company or model.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units must support secure remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Manufacturers must retrofit already-installed units to support the function within 6 years of this standard taking effect, prioritizing units subject to an active safety notice or elevated risk. Where a retrofit is not technically feasible, the manufacturer must provide an equivalent risk-reduction measure and notify the regulator and affected customers.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression no later than 36 months after this standard is adopted. The suppression system must be appropriate to the battery chemistry and designed to reduce fire spread and protect occupants and nearby properties.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices promptly when credible information indicates a risk involving their model, including the nature of the risk, affected units, actions customers should take, and available support. A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Manufacturers must notify the regulator within 5 business days of identifying that threshold has been exceeded and promptly notify affected customers; the regulator may require immediate protective measures pending completion of the recall.

document.section_notes: S2 was the decisive concession: the 5% limit is kept only as a safety action level, with no mandatory sales stop and open-ended continued sale during remediation, which protects Northwind's 6.2% Hearth 10. S5 keeps a mandatory recall at 8 per 100,000 with no transition or corrective-action alternative, which exposes Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9) to immediate recall. S1 is strong (24-hour reporting of all thermal incidents regardless of cause confirmation), and S3 and S4 sit inside the acceptable ranges at 6 years and 36 months respectively. The S5 'promptly' notice wording is acceptable but not numeric.
